scope: B05-19 OA55–OA59 independent local source review

groups.contract: Ordinary outer method, not itself a generator: construct comparison key (exact crossing event slot 2, actual confirmation, negative integer First), then capture range_start.tzinfo. No parent fields inspected on native route. No direction-sensitive comparator or price arithmetic introduced here. Attribute/key creation and capture occur before fallback or local build try blocks; capture failures propagate.

Native time requires exact datetime type, then tzinfo object identity with captured native timezone (including None); short-circuit before tzinfo access for non-exact type. No subclass admission, timezone normalization, offset computation, value-equality timezone substitution or fold check. Exact native shape is not proof of comparability or of a coherent chronological domain.

Build the four-field tuple eagerly in order: reaction number, source index, reaction First, reaction Break; both getattr evaluations precede all exact-int predicates. Boolean and subclasses fail exact type. Only after all four pass, validate actual confirmation then source time, exact Decimal then is_finite, and finally crossing None or exact tuple of length at least three, exact-int main index, native main timestamp and exact event. Extra crossing slots retained, not validated. No positivity/bounds, reaction concrete-type, direction, price/source coherence or crossing chronology test in validator. Index/attribute/property errors may occur even when an earlier tuple element would fail. Validation is called inside build try, not again during consumption.

If query stop fails native-time gate, synchronously invoke OA53 then obtain iterator from its complete returned list; this is not delayed until consumption. OA53 cache hit may avoid geometry materialization. OA53's permissive legacy gates and exceptions remain operative, not normalized by this route.

Read optional initial view default None. Only None rebuilds; force OA45 initial record materialization outside try and before accepted ledger reads, preserving that eager failure boundary. OA45 itself may compute and cache all records/crossings using caller context; errors propagate without publishing initial False here. Within try/localcontext, construct every OA46 match with accepted-live singleton and None creation, then validate all before selecting non-null crossing strictly after own confirmation. Sort stably by main key. Build physical identity to (cross,confirmation) map using first insertion; differing pair for same identity raises, equal pair accepted even if other fields differ. Store sorted matches, aligned crossing times and geometry map on success; caught Exception publishes False, then eager OA53 fallback. False is sticky in this method; no rebuild on False. Local Decimal context copies caller settings, isolates flag changes for its enclosed operations only; it does not wrap OA45, fallback or consumption. This preserves a specific initial materialization ordering, not all eager exception precedence (OA53 may have a cached result and converts selected initial matches only).

Read published audit view and pending list eagerly. Refresh on audit None or truthy pending; full confirmation index only for None, otherwise pending. Inside try and localcontext allocate new match list and reference initial geometry. No refresh with dict and empty pending; False with empty pending falls back. If False has pending, refresh can enter and eventually False.copy fails if reached, caught below. Normal index owner on non-dict resets audit to None instead of appending. Index inputs are referenced, not copied before validation; no concurrent-mutation guarantee.

For each selected index tuple, unpack confirmation, First, Break; validate native indexed time and exact int keys in short-circuit order. Ledger lookup exact unconverted key, require exact dict (missing row None fails rather than silently skipping optimized view). Read stop level via required key; accept exact Decimal,str,int,float only (not bool/subclasses); as_decimal preserves Decimal else converts str representation. Build nine-slot match in source order using required number, reaction, actual confirmation, normalized level, required source index/time, optional crossing via get, accepted-live singleton, None creation. Validate native match then indexed confirmation equality; malformed/unresolved key or row leads caught failure, not a local skip. No equality check between indexed First/Break and reaction physical pair, no identity bound check. No rounding imposed; caller context is copied for build only.

Null stored crossing requires key (actual confirmation, normalized level) present in crossing cache with value exactly None; otherwise raise and fall back. Known-null row is omitted; no crossing recomputation or writeback in native build. Non-null crossing included only if event strictly after own confirmation; equality and earlier events omitted. For included rows, compare event pair with initial physical identity map; conflict triggers fallback because eager dictionary replacement retains first-insertion rank. Agreement tests only event pair, not source/price/number; audit-audit conflicting geometry is not checked. Append keyed match using main key extended by indexed First and Break; physical identity used for conflict lookup may differ from index pair if malformed. No parent stop/reset filter during build.

Use empty audit dict on full build, else shallow copy current mapping. If nonempty new rows, stable sort by full key; tier is bit_length of row count (not exact equal length or a fixed capacity). While tier already exists, pop older run from candidate map, merge older before newer by full key, materialize a fresh list and recompute tier. Store fresh rows and aligned crossing-time projection. Never mutate old published run lists or map in this build; nested match objects remain shared and not frozen. Equal full keys within a merge select older run first; equal keys across distinct tiers depend on audit mapping insertion order in OA59, not an unconditional global insertion-rank proof. Any Exception in try sets candidate audit False; BaseException and failures before/after try are not caught. Clear pending on success or caught failure before assigning published audit (failure discards pending but canonical ledger/index retained). If False then synchronously call eager OA53 and return iterator; exceptions there propagate. An external alias mutation can violate run immutability; no deep copy or lock.

Unpack initial view; compute upper bound of parent stop in sorted reset-time array; read earliest reset strictly later than stop or None. Reset equal parent stop excluded. This captures query-time reset once before returning generator; reset search/comparison errors propagate outside build try. Reset setter clears eager result cache but does not mutate already-issued generator's captured reset.

Generator eligibility on consumption: right-bisect aligned crossing times at parent stop; iterate suffix with original position order, unwrap audit row iff flag truthy. First crossing >= captured reset terminates run, including equality, relying on sorted crossing times. Yield only actual confirmation strictly > parent stop, retaining original keyed audit row or initial match. No cross>confirmation recheck, no geometry/cause/level/type check, no copy. Bisect/index/comparison/iteration exceptions occur during consumption and cannot trigger OA55 build fallback.

Return generator object; consumption creates eligible iterators for audit runs in mapping insertion order, merges by stored full key, unwraps matches, then merges initial stream first and audit stream second by main key. Equal main key takes initial before audit; within initial stable ordering and within audit full key determine ties; equal full keys across runs follow run order. Fresh seen set per iterator; compute actual reaction physical int pair at consumption, add before yielding first occurrence, suppress later duplicates without provenance union or ledger writes. This selects minimum eligible key for a coherent immutable stream, not a general eager dictionary insertion-rank equivalent under malformed/inconsistent identities. Merge initialization and advancement may read keys/raise before a particular row is yielded. Consumer may stop early; later rows/errors never observed. Captured local map/run references are retained across owner replacement but shared nested objects are not frozen. No eager result cache publication on native path.

findings.description: Expanded OA55–OA59 active specification for eager outer vs lazy inner timing, exact native shape/order, initial materialization/Decimal context boundaries, geometry and index coherence gaps, null cache, fallback state transitions, stable tier/run ordering, snapshot aliasing, strict bisects, consumption errors, physical deduplication and caller reordering. No production defect or runtime equivalence asserted.

limitations: Native exact types, timezone identity and finite Decimal do not establish universal comparability, stable attributes, bounded identities, chronology coherence, or same value/side effects under unusual inputs.

Eager OA53 can include equal indexed confirmation with identity beyond signed 63-bit sentinel or row confirmation inconsistent with index; native strict actual confirmation and coherence gate differ. Native rejects/validates unselected rows on build, while eager may skip them; fallback is synchronous and may read cache. Native null crossing requires cached None rather than recomputing. Caller-context vs localcontext flags/traps, eager exception timing and lazy consumption are not proven equivalent.

Initial conflicting event pairs and initial/audit event conflicts trigger conservative fallback; audit-audit conflicts or index-versus-reaction identity inconsistency are not expressly checked. Equal event pairs can differ in non-key fields. OA53 preserves first insertion rank even after replacement; OA59 selects first merged physical identity. Equal complete audit keys across tiers use run order; stable tie equivalence depends on owner invariants, not claimed for arbitrary malformed data.

Published audit containers are copied/replaced, not deeply immutable; already issued generator captures view and reset, but nested aliases remain mutable. Owner append/rebuild/reset and caller early termination are bounded source observations, not cross-owner certification.

Source-first local review by GPT, not independently staffed. No trading execution, RAW payload, ZIP, production changes, performance measurements, fresh AST generator, or independent SHA-256 claim. Static inventory validated against pinned historical canonical arrays, actual source line review, CP316 and historical W1 crosswalk.
